questions.prompt: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed with graphite electrodes. What forms at the cathode?
questions.explanation: Positive $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ ions move to the negative cathode and gain electrons: $\text{Pb}^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Pb}$. Bromine forms at the anode.

questions.prompt: Which of these are electrolytes? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: An electrolyte has ions that are free to move. Sugar is made of molecules, not ions. In solid sodium chloride the ions are fixed in place, so it does not conduct.

questions.prompt: In electrolysis, the anode is the positive electrode.
questions.explanation: The anode is positive and attracts negative ions (anions); the cathode is negative and attracts positive ions (cations).

questions.prompt: Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed and 40 cm³ of hydrogen is collected at the cathode. What volume of oxygen, in cm³, is collected at the anode at the same time?
questions.explanation: 4 electrons make 2 molecules of $\text{H}_2$ but only 1 molecule of $\text{O}_2$, so the volumes are in the ratio 2 : 1. Oxygen $= 40 \div 2 = 20$ cm³.

questions.prompt: A current of 1.0 A flows through copper(II) sulfate solution for 9 650 s. What mass of copper, in grams, is deposited on the cathode? (Cu = 64; 1 mol of electrons carries 96 500 C)
questions.explanation: $Q = It = 1.0 \times 9650 = 9650$ C. Moles of electrons $= \frac{9650}{96\,500} = 0.10$ mol. $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}$, so moles of Cu $= 0.10 \div 2 = 0.050$ mol. Mass $= 0.050 \times 64 = 3.2$ g.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the process that uses electrolysis to coat an object, such as a moto handlebar, with a thin layer of metal?
questions.explanation: This is **electroplating**. The object is made the cathode, and the electrolyte contains ions of the plating metal.
